title: Pushforward of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes, with coefficient rings $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$
([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]) and categories of module objects
$\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]). The *pushforward of module objects* is

$$
f_*:=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y},
$$

where the transport ([def-sfb-modobj-transport]) $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)$ makes $f^{\Ab}_*M$ an
$f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X$-module through the lax monoidal structure of the pushforward
$f^{\Ab}_*$ of abelian sheaves ([def-sfb-finite-lower-star],
[def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal]), and $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}$ restricts scalars
([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]) along $\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]). Thus the underlying sheaf of $f_*M$ is
$f^{\Ab}_*M$, and $\Lambda_Y$ acts by

$$
\Lambda_Y\otimes f^{\Ab}_*M\xrightarrow{\eta_f\otimes1}
f^{\Ab}_*\Lambda_X\otimes f^{\Ab}_*M\xrightarrow{\mu}
f^{\Ab}_*(\Lambda_X\otimes M)\to f^{\Ab}_*M .
$$

The functor $f_*$ is additive and left exact.

proof.text: Put $F=f^{\Ab}_*$. The lax monoidal structure of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal] and [def-sfb-modobj-transport] give an $F\Lambda_X$-module with underlying sheaf $FM$ and action $F\gamma_M\circ\mu^F_{\Lambda_X,M}$. The coefficient map $\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to F\Lambda_X$ is a ring morphism by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Apply [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] to it. The resulting action is $F\gamma_M\circ\mu^F_{\Lambda_X,M}\circ(\eta_f\otimes FM)$, exactly the displayed formula; the resulting functor has underlying sheaf $FM$ and sends a module morphism $a$ to $Fa$.

source.place: Construction: transport, then restriction; underlying sheaf and displayed action

proof.text: Tensoring preserves colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], hence zero objects and binary coproducts. Such a functor preserves the biproduct projections (characterized by identity and zero on each summand), and thus diagonals and codiagonals; applying it to $a+b=\nabla\circ(a\oplus b)\circ\Delta$ proves additivity of tensoring. The linearity equation in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is then closed under sums, negatives and zero by bilinearity of composition, so module Hom groups inherit these operations from the underlying abelian sheaves. By the restriction formula of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], for module maps $a,b\colon M\to N$ and $V\in Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, $(F(a+b))_V=(a+b)_{V\times_YX}=a_{V\times_YX}+b_{V\times_YX}=(Fa+Fb)_V$. Restriction of scalars leaves underlying maps unchanged ([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]), so this equality proves $f_*(a+b)=f_*a+f_*b$; the zero map is treated by the same formula. Thus $f_*$ is additive.

source.place: First sentence: both factors are additive, expanded on sections

proof.text: The adjunction of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], with coefficient category $\Ab$, implies that $F$ preserves zero objects, finite products and kernels directly: for any such underlying sheaf limit $L=\lim_i M_i$ and any abelian sheaf $T$ on $Y$, the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(T,FL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*_{\Ab}T,L)\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(f^*_{\Ab}T,M_i)\cong\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(T,FM_i)$ are exactly the universal property of the image cone. Here finite products and kernels of abelian sheaves exist sectionwise: compatible families of sections in a product glue component by component, and compatible sections killed by a morphism glue to a section still killed by it. In particular $F$ preserves zero objects, finite products, and kernels.

source.place: Second sentence: the abelian-sheaf pushforward is left exact because it is a right adjoint

proof.text: In each abelian-sheaf category tensoring is additive by step 2, so [lem-sfb-modobj-kernels] applies to every module morphism: its kernel is the sheaf kernel with the unique action making the kernel inclusion linear. Applying $f_*$ to a kernel inclusion gives a linear map by step 1 whose underlying map is a kernel by step 3. The uniqueness of the kernel action and its module-kernel universal property in [lem-sfb-modobj-kernels] therefore show that this image inclusion is a module kernel. Thus $f_*$ preserves kernels.

source.place: Third sentence: kernel actions and their universal property give preservation of kernels

proof.text: For a ring object $R$ in either abelian-sheaf category, finite products of $R$-module objects have their underlying sheaf products: give $P=\prod_i M_i$ the action uniquely characterized by $p_i\gamma_P=\gamma_{M_i}(R\otimes p_i)$. Composing each unit or associativity equation with $p_i$ gives the corresponding axiom of $M_i$ in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], so the product projections jointly imply the action laws. For linear maps $u_i\colon T\to M_i$, the unique underlying map $u\colon T\to P$ is linear because $p_i u\gamma_T=u_i\gamma_T=\gamma_{M_i}(R\otimes u_i)=p_i\gamma_P(R\otimes u)$ for every $i$. For an empty index set $P=0$, and the action, its laws, and the universal factorization are unique.

source.place: Third sentence: construction and universal property of finite products of module objects

proof.text: The product comparison $e\colon f_*(\prod_i M_i)\to\prod_i f_*M_i$ has linear components, hence is linear by step 5, and its underlying sheaf map is invertible by step 3. Its underlying inverse is linear: from $e\gamma_P=\gamma_Q(R\otimes e)$, compose on the left with $e^{-1}$ and on the right with $R\otimes e^{-1}$ to obtain $\gamma_P(R\otimes e^{-1})=e^{-1}\gamma_Q$. These inverse maps therefore form a module isomorphism. This includes the empty product, so $f_*$ preserves finite products and the zero object.

source.place: Third and fourth sentences: product comparisons are module isomorphisms

proof.text: For a finite diagram $D$, put $P=\prod_i D_i$ and $Q=\prod_{a\colon i\to j}D_j$, with maps $s,t\colon P\to Q$ characterized in the $a$ component by $s_a=D(a)p_i$ and $t_a=p_j$. A map $u\colon T\to P$ satisfies $(s-t)u=0$ exactly when its components form a cone on $D$; hence the kernel of $s-t$ with its projected maps is the diagram limit. Applying $f_*$ preserves the products by step 6, the difference by step 2, and the kernel by step 4, so the image cone has this same universal property. Thus $f_*$ preserves finite limits and is left exact.

source.place: Third and fourth sentences: explicit finite-diagram limit construction and preservation

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, with the additivity and finite-limit arguments expanded
